blocks.prompt: 16 (i) If \(a, b, c\) are in H.P., show that \(\frac{a - b}{b - c} = \frac{a}{c}\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof. Since \(a, b, c\) are in H.P., \(b\) is the H.M. of \(a\) and \(c\): \(b = \frac{2ac}{a + c}\).
Plan: compute \(a - b\) and \(b - c\) with this value and divide.
steps:
Given: \(a, b, c\) in H.P. (\(a \ne c\), \(a + c \ne 0\)).
To prove: \(\frac{a - b}{b - c} = \frac{a}{c}\).
Method: Replace \(b\) by \(\frac{2ac}{a + c}\).

Find \(a - b\)
\[a - b = a - \dfrac{2ac}{a + c}\]
\[= \dfrac{a^{2} + ac - 2ac}{a + c}\]
\[= \dfrac{a(a - c)}{a + c}\]
Why: Common denominator \(a + c\); take \(a\) common.

Find \(b - c\)
\[b - c = \dfrac{2ac}{a + c} - c\]
\[= \dfrac{2ac - ac - c^{2}}{a + c}\]
\[= \dfrac{c(a - c)}{a + c}\]
Why: Same method; take \(c\) common.

Divide
\[\dfrac{a - b}{b - c} = \dfrac{a(a - c)}{c(a - c)}\]
\[= \dfrac{a}{c}\]
Why: The factors \(a + c\) and \(a - c\) cancel.

blocks.prompt: 16 (ii) If \(a, b, c\) are in H.P., show that \((a - c)^{2} = (a + c)(a - 2b + c)\).
blocks.explanation:
Again use \(b = \frac{2ac}{a + c}\), so \(2b(a + c) = 4ac\).
Plan: expand the right side as \((a + c)^{2} - 2b(a + c)\) and simplify to \((a - c)^{2}\).
steps:
Given: \(a, b, c\) in H.P. (\(a + c \ne 0\)).
To prove: \((a - c)^{2} = (a + c)(a - 2b + c)\).
Method: Start from the right side and use \(b(a + c) = 2ac\).

Rewrite the right side
\[(a + c)(a - 2b + c)\]
\[= (a + c)\big[(a + c) - 2b\big]\]
\[= (a + c)^{2} - 2b(a + c)\]
Why: Group \(a + c\) inside the bracket and multiply out.

Use the H.P. condition
\[b = \dfrac{2ac}{a + c}\]
\[\Rightarrow 2b(a + c) = 4ac\]
Why: Multiply \(b(a + c) = 2ac\) by 2.

Simplify
\[(a + c)^{2} - 4ac\]
\[= a^{2} + 2ac + c^{2} - 4ac\]
\[= a^{2} - 2ac + c^{2}\]
\[= (a - c)^{2}\]
Why: Expand the square and collect the \(ac\) terms.

Conclude and check
\[(a + c)(a - 2b + c) = (a - c)^{2}\]
Check with \(a = 1, b = \frac{1}{2}, c = \frac{1}{3}\): left \(\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{2} = \frac{4}{9}\); right \(\frac{4}{3}\left(1 - 1 + \frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{4}{9}\) \(\checkmark\).
